## Context

A GHA audit on 2026-09-29 found two workflows failing on every run:

- **`rxiv-paper-eval.yaml`** (weekly, Tuesday): 9 consecutive scheduled failures from 2026-08-04 to 2026-09-29. The last success was 2026-07-28 (run 30348484489). `docs/research/rxiv-agentic-papers.md` has received no new papers since.

GitHub Models was fully retired on 2026-07-30: ["The playground, model catalog, inference API, and bring your own key (BYOK) are no longer available"](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-30-github-models-is-now-retired/). Both reusable actions call that endpoint:

- `qte77/gha-issue-triage` v0.3.0, pinned `4a07dd2`. Upstream #109 (HTTP 410 Gone) and #110.

The failures show up as `50/50 LLM calls failed` (08-25 to 09-15) and as an uncaught `JSONDecodeError` on an empty response body (09-22, 09-29 run 36547529097).

## Proposed

1. Upstream: migrate both actions to a live provider (GitHub's changelog names Microsoft Foundry or GitHub Copilot models; an OpenAI-compatible provider via secret is another option), and handle empty or 410 responses with a clear error.
2. Here: bump both pins once fixed upstream, then trigger one `rxiv-paper-eval` run (never two on the same day, per CONTRIBUTING) to backfill.

title: GitHub Models retired 2026-07-30 - default LLM path is dead
text:
GitHub Models was fully retired on **2026-07-30**. The playground, model catalog, inference API, and BYOK are gone for everyone, including existing customers with active usage. There is no grace period and no graceful degradation - calls to the endpoint hard-fail.

Timeline (primary sources):
- 2026-06-16 closed to new customers: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-06-16-github-models-is-no-longer-available-to-new-customers/
- 2026-07-01 full retirement announced for 2026-07-30, with brownouts on 07-16 and 07-23: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-01-github-models-is-being-fully-retired-on-july-30-2026/
- 2026-07-30 retired: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-30-github-models-is-now-retired/

## What breaks here

`src/llm.py:9,20,23-43` - `_call_github_models` posts to `https://models.github.ai/inference/chat/completions`, and `MODEL` defaults to `openai/gpt-4.1`.

`call_llm()` already falls back to Anthropic when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, but **GitHub Models is the default path**. Any consumer that has not explicitly configured `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is broken today: the triage step exhausts its 3 retries and raises `RuntimeError`, failing the workflow run.

Note the `models: read` Actions permission itself does not error - only the endpoint call does. Affected workflows therefore look correctly configured while failing.

## Smallest viable fix

This is a **default flip, not new code** - the fallback already exists. Swap the precedence so Anthropic (or an `OPENAI_API_BASE`-compatible path, already scoped as Path B in `docs/integrations.md`) is the default, since…

title: chore(ci): adopt qte77/.github reusable release workflows
text:
## Adopt the `qte77/.github` reusable release workflows

`qte77/.github` is adding reusable `workflow_call` release workflows — landing in
[PR #33](https://github.com/qte77/.github/pull/33) (tracking qte77/.github#32). This repo is set
up for `bump-my-version`, so it's a candidate to drop its inline/ad-hoc release steps and call the
shared workflows via `uses:` once the PR merges.

### What to adopt
- **Bump** — `qte77/.github/.github/workflows/bump-version.yml` (signed-commit-via-GitHub-API;
  opt-in `use_uv` / `sync_lockfile` / `collect_scriv` inputs).
- **Tag** — `qte77/.github/.github/workflows/tag-release.yml` (watches the version file on `main`,
  creates the annotated `v{version}` tag).
- **Publish** — `qte77/.github/.github/workflows/publish-release.yml` (GitHub Release from the
  `CHANGELOG.md ## [version]` notes).

### Thin-caller sketch
```yaml
# .github/workflows/tag-release.yml
on: { push: { branches: [main], paths: [pyproject.toml] } }
jobs:
  tag:
    uses: qte77/.github/.github/workflows/tag-release.yml@main
    permissions: { contents: write }
# bump + publish are workflow_dispatch callers that `uses:` the matching reusable.
```

### Guardrails (do not violate)
- **Never delete tags/releases on any failure path** — release immutability remembers deleted tag
  names forever (`HTTP 422 GH013`), permanently burning the version number. See qte77/.github#23.
- Tag/publish are **idempotent** — abort if the tag/Release already exists; never overwrite.
- **scriv** is the estate-standard changelog tool (fragments in `changelog.d/`, collected on bump).

title: feat: set descriptions on auto-created labels (feature, needs-discussion)
text:
## Problem

When the triage action applies labels like \`feature\` or \`needs-discussion\` to a repo that hasn't pre-created them with a description, GitHub creates them with **no description**. Downstream this:

- Makes the label picker noisy (mystery labels next to well-described GitHub defaults).
- Forces repo owners to manually add descriptions after the fact.

Caught while auditing labels on \`qte77/analyze-stock-kpi\`: \`feature\` and \`needs-discussion\` were both label-described-empty, while \`enhancement\` (a GitHub default) was self-describing.

When the action creates a label that doesn't yet exist on the target repo (or even when it just applies an existing one), set a sensible default description if the current description is empty. Suggested wording matching GitHub's default style:

| Label | Description |
|---|---|
| \`feature\` | New capability / feature request |
| \`needs-discussion\` | Requires further discussion before action |
| \`good-first-issue\` | Good for newcomers |
| \`enhancement\` | Improvement to existing functionality |
| \`bug\` | Something isn't working |
| \`duplicate\` | This issue or pull request already exists |
| \`invalid\` | This doesn't seem right |

(The GitHub-default ones — \`bug\`, \`enhancement\`, \`duplicate\`, \`invalid\` — already arrive self-described if the repo never customized them.)

title: refactor(config): centralize env-var config into pydantic-settings AppSettings
text:
## Problem

8 `getenv()` calls scattered across `src/`:

| File | Variable |
| --- | --- |
| `src/app.py` | `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`, `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` |
| `src/comment.py` | `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` |
| `src/llm.py` | `AI_TOKEN`, `MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_BASE` |
| `src/duplicates.py` (or other) | `MAX_DUPLICATES`, `SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` |

No central listing; no type coercion (`MAX_DUPLICATES` and `SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` need manual `int()`/`float()`); no validation. Adding a new setting means hunting for the pattern across files.

## Proposed solution — `pydantic-settings` AppSettings

Adopt the section-3 pattern from `py-harden-ruff.md`:

```python
# src/config.py
from pathlib import Path
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict


class AppSettings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(frozen=True)

    # LLM backend
    ai_token: str = ""
    model: str = "openai/gpt-4.1"
    anthropic_api_key: str = ""
    openai_api_base: str = ""

    # Duplicate detection
    max_duplicates: int = 10
    similarity_threshold: float = 0.6

    # GitHub Actions context
    github_event_name: str = ""
    github_event_path: Path | None = None
    github_repository: str = ""


settings = AppSettings()  # module-level singleton
```

Consumers: `from src.config import settings; settings.max_duplicates`.

## Effects

- + Typed config (int, float, Path) instead of `str` + manual coercion
- + Single source of truth; new settings discoverable in one file
- + Env-var override flows through with zero plumbing (already free via `getenv()`, but now…

title: feat: detect evidence-library drift (gapNarrative and other fields change wording across rebuilds)
text:
evidence-library.json's fields (gapNarrative most visibly) are not append-only -- rebuilding the library changes their wording, and nothing detects or flags this. Confirmed two independent ways during arc-011: (1) grounding_warnings calibration against the real 34-pack corpus found the same specific numbers (2,100, 96.3%, 85%, 98%) repeated verbatim across many independently-tailored packs from different companies, none present in the current library -- strong evidence of real content from an older snapshot; (2) several retrofit subagents independently found existing gap-report.md files quoting gapNarrative text no longer present in the current field (e.g. a database/message-queue framing that has since been dropped or reworded). Impact today: grounding_warnings permanently flags ~37 numbers across the corpus that are legitimate historical content, not hallucinations, with no way to distinguish "stale but was true" from "never grounded" -- and a human reading an old gap-report.md has no signal that a quoted "gapNarrative says X" may no longer be accurate. Possible approach: hash or version-stamp evidence-library.json at build time, record which stamp a pack was tailored against (this overlaps with #365/#366's broader "pack has no source" problem but is specifically about the evidence-library dependency, not the tailor-result JSON), and/or a lightweight `ajoa-kit evidence-diff <old> <new>` reporting which top-level fields changed so a human rebuilding the library gets a diff summary before old packs go stale silently.

title: Decide: should enhanced-kpi-screener longs/shorts derive from best/worst (ADR-0014 open question)
text:
## Decision needed

Owner rule (2026-09-24): *"the aggregated and long/short candidates lists have to just copy the best/worst candidates resp calculate the candidates using the same original data!"*

#408 (ADR-0014, amending ADR-0013 D2) implemented this for:
- the aggregated best/worst lists (now written from the same source-universe records the ranking used; no second fetch);
- the dashboard's current long/short candidates (sourced from the aggregated best/worst lists; the point-in-time 6-input score is kept only for scoring past dates in the backtest).

**Left open by ADR-0014:** `enhanced-kpi-screener-longs` / `-shorts` (`src/analyze_stock_kpi/orchestrators/enhanced_kpi_screener_longshort.py`) use a **conjunctive-gate** selection, not `screener_score` ranking. After #408 they reuse the source data (no refetch) but are **not** a subset of best/worst.

## Options

- **(a) Copy:** longs = best-N, shorts = worst-N by `screener_score`. One method everywhere; retires the gate methodology.
- **(b) Keep the gates, same data:** status quo after #408. Label the lists clearly as a different methodology.
- **(c) Gate within best/worst:** apply the gates only inside best (longs) / worst (shorts), so the result is a subset of each while keeping the gate signal.

Recommended default: **(c)**. It satisfies "copy/derive from best/worst" and keeps the extra signal. Implement test-first, and record it in an ADR amendment.

## Adopt the `qte77/.github` reusable release workflows

`qte77/.github` is adding reusable `workflow_call` release workflows — landing in
[PR #33](https://github.com/qte77/.github/pull/33) (tracking qte77/.github#32). This repo is set
up for `bump-my-version`, so it's a candidate to drop its inline/ad-hoc release steps and call the
shared workflows via `uses:` once the PR merges.

### What to adopt
- **Bump** — `qte77/.github/.github/workflows/bump-version.yml` (signed-commit-via-GitHub-API;
  opt-in `use_uv` / `sync_lockfile` / `collect_scriv` inputs).
- **Tag** — `qte77/.github/.github/workflows/tag-release.yml` (watches the version file on `main`,
  creates the annotated `v{version}` tag).
- **Publish** — `qte77/.github/.github/workflows/publish-release.yml` (GitHub Release from the
  `CHANGELOG.md ## [version]` notes).

### Thin-caller sketch
```yaml
# .github/workflows/tag-release.yml
on: { push: { branches: [main], paths: [pyproject.toml] } }
jobs:
  tag:
    uses: qte77/.github/.github/workflows/tag-release.yml@main
    permissions: { contents: write }
# bump + publish are workflow_dispatch callers that `uses:` the matching reusable.
```

### Guardrails (do not violate)
- **Never delete tags/releases on any failure path** — release immutability remembers deleted tag
  names forever (`HTTP 422 GH013`), permanently burning the version number. See qte77/.github#23.
- Tag/publish are **idempotent** — abort if the tag/Release already exists; never overwrite.
- **scriv** is the estate-standard changelog tool (fragments in `changelog.d/`, collected on bump).

title: feat(skill): add `/observe` — capture-and-attach-only skill, no VLM in the loop
text:
## Problem

For many \"show me what's on the screen\" workflows the user does not need a token-cheap text summary — they want **Claude itself** to look at the actual pixels. Today the only path is:

1. Manually run `flameshot` / `gnome-screenshot` / `screencapture` etc.
2. Manually drag the resulting file into the CC conversation.

That works but is fiddly. The plugin already owns the cross-platform screen-capture problem (today via `mss`, soon multi-backend per #119). Wrapping that capture in a slash command with no VLM in the loop is the smallest reasonable affordance.

## Proposed scope

New skill, `skills/observe/SKILL.md` + `src/cc_observe/` (or fold into `cc_vlm` if simpler). Behaviour:

```
/observe [--template terminal|editor|...]   # template is optional, just labels the attachment
```

What it does:

1. Grab the screen using the existing capture layer (`cc_vlm.capture.ScreenCapture` — same module that powers `/see`).
2. Run the same preprocessing as `/see` (max_dimension 768, JPEG quality 85) to keep attachments small.
3. Write the JPEG to a temp path.
4. Return the image as a tool result so CC can attach it to the conversation. **No local VLM is invoked.**

That's it. Single skill, single entry point, ~50 LoC.

## How is this different from issue #121 (\`ClaudeVisionEngine\`)?

- #121 keeps `/see`'s mental model (one skill, swappable engines including Claude's vision) — the user still configures `[vlm]` and thinks in terms of \"the VLM\".
- This skill (`/observe`) has **zero VLM mental model**. No engine knob, no `model_path`, no `handler_name`, no `setup_see`…

## Problem

`/see` currently requires installing a local VLM (`llama-cpp-python` wheel, ~3.75 GB GGUF model, hardware-specific build) before it can do anything. Reproduced 2026-05-15: a fresh `setup_default_all` + Moondream2-F16 install pegged a 4-core laptop for over a minute on a single screenshot description.

text:
## Problem

When `.cc-senses.toml` is malformed, the `/see`, `/speak`, `/listen` CLIs dump a 14-line Python traceback instead of one user-actionable line. Reproduced 2026-05-15 with a duplicate `[vlm]` section:

```
$ make see_file FILE=...
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<frozen runpy>", line 198, in _run_module_as_main
  ...
tomllib.TOMLDecodeError: Cannot overwrite a value (at line 48, column 92)
```

All three CLIs share the same code path through `cc_voice_common.config.load_toml_section` at `src/cc_voice_common/config.py:29`, so this fixes once for all three.

| Exception | Today | Should say |
|---|---|---|
| `tomllib.TOMLDecodeError` | full traceback | `cc_vlm: .cc-senses.toml: <message>. Often a duplicate [section] or repeated key.` |

| `pydantic.ValidationError` (e.g. wrong type, unknown engine) | full traceback | `cc_vlm: [vlm] config invalid — <field>: <pydantic message>.` |

title: feat(vlm): multi-backend screen capture — native tools for Linux/macOS, mss as fallback
text:
## Problem

`src/cc_vlm/capture.py` currently hard-codes `mss.mss()` for all platforms. `mss` uses `XGetImage` on Linux, which fails outright on:

- **Wayland sessions** (the default on Fedora 43+, Ubuntu 24.04+, recent Arch) — `XGetImage()` returns nothing, the error surfaces as `cc_vlm: screen capture failed: XGetImage() failed`.
- **Headless / SSH** sessions without X forwarding.
- **Sandboxed contexts** (Claude Code's bwrap, containers without display access).

macOS support via `mss` works but is slower than Apple's built-in `screencapture` binary and doesn't expose Retina/multi-display nuances cleanly.

Reproduced 2026-05-15 on Fedora 43 / GNOME Wayland:

- `make see` → `mss XGetImage() failed`
- `gnome-screenshot -f /tmp/cap.png` → falls back to X11, then crashes (`Unable to capture a screenshot of any window`) because GNOME Shell's D-Bus Screenshot interface isn't reachable in the sub-shell.
- `flameshot full -p /tmp/cap.png` → ✅ works (uses `xdg-desktop-portal`).

No single tool works in every environment. Capture is genuinely environment-fragile on Linux.

## Proposed scope

Refactor `cc_vlm.capture.ScreenCapture` to a small strategy pattern. Same public signature (`grab(monitor: int = 0) -> PIL.Image.Image`); pluggable backend underneath.

### Detection order (first match wins)

1. **Explicit override** — `CC_VLM_CAPTURE_BACKEND` env var or `[vlm] capture_backend` TOML key. Values: `screencapture` | `grim` | `gnome-screenshot` | `spectacle` | `scrot` | `flameshot` | `mss`.
2. **Auto-detect** by `platform.system()` + `$XDG_SESSION_TYPE` +…

title: ~/.claude.json has no rebuild-persistence mechanism (unlike ~/.claude)
text:
## Problem

`~/.claude` is now symlinked into persisted storage on rebuild (qte77/polyforge-orchestrator#82, #202), but `~/.claude.json` — a sibling file holding per-project trust approvals and marketplace/onboarding state — has no equivalent. It's wiped on every container rebuild.

Symlinking it like a directory is unsafe: Claude Code's config writes aren't verified atomic-rename-safe on every path, which silently breaks a *file* symlink (unlike a directory symlink, which isn't affected). See #199 failure mode 1, which hit this exact pattern for `settings.json`.

## Scope

Narrower than #199 (single-machine rebuild survival, not cross-machine git-backed history). A copy-based restore-on-missing + periodic sync might be the safe shape, but that design work hasn't been done — opening this to track the gap, not propose a fix yet.

title: Proposal: session-archive — durable ~/.claude snapshot + restore (cc-meta corpus survives rebuilds)
text:
## Problem

`cc-meta` builds on session history — `summarizing-session-end` writes to `~/.claude/session-summaries/`, `bigpicture` synthesises across it, `mining-session-patterns` reads transcripts. On Codespaces (and any devcontainer) `~/.claude` lives in the container layer and is destroyed on rebuild, so that corpus resets to empty and the synthesis silently starts from nothing.

`qte77/dotfiles` covers part of this (`~/.claude` → `/workspaces/.claude-files/` symlink, which survives rebuilds on one account). What it doesn't give you is history: what a transcript said, when a learning was actually formed, or any of it on a second machine. qte77/qte77#165 hits the same wall from another direction and ends up using an issue body as the backup store.

## Proposal

A session-archive capability — snapshot `~/.claude` to git on `SessionEnd`, restore it on a fresh machine. `cc-meta` looks like the natural host since it already owns a `SessionEnd` hook and consumes exactly this data, but it could equally be its own plugin.

I've had an implementation running for a day (~20 commits, 19 transcripts, 16 MB) and would rather contribute it than have it live in one private repo. Shape:

- **Deny-by-default allowlist** — `projects/`, `history.jsonl`, `settings.json`, `scripts/`, `session-summaries/`, `plans/`, `todos/`. Nothing else is copied, so widening is a deliberate edit.
- **Never stored** — `.credentials.json`, `sessions/*.key`, `shell-snapshots/` (exported env), `ide/`, `cache/`, and raw `~/.claude.json` (it carries `oauthAccount` and MCP server env). A sanitised…

title: Promote learning: stuck CodeFactor ERROR clears via update-to-main, not nudge commits
text:
Candidate shared rule/skill for this marketplace (surfaced in qte77/qte77 `AGENT_LEARNINGS.md`, PRs #158/#159).

**Pattern:** a required `CodeFactor` status check can get stuck at `ERROR` (null description / empty target URL) on a head SHA and block PR merges — seen on docs-only PRs.

**Anti-pattern:** empty "nudge CI" commits do NOT clear it (the stuck SHA keeps its errored status) and pollute history.

**Fix:** bring the branch up to date with the default branch (`gh pr update-branch <n>` or local `git merge origin/main`) — the fresh, GitHub-signed SHA gets a clean re-analysis that goes green.

**Why shared:** CodeFactor gates many estate repos, so agents in any of them hit this. Pairs with the existing rule: never `--admin` past a genuinely failing/absent check (only the signature gate is bypassable).

text:
## Gap

Every security skill in the marketplace **produces** findings (`auditing-code-security`, `detecting-secrets`, `scanning-dependencies`, mas-design's `securing-mas`). None **consumes and verifies** a third-party or AI-generated security report — a fast-growing genre (automated agent-pipeline teardowns, scanner PDFs, bug-bounty submissions).

An 11-agent "Agentic Security Agent" MITRE ATLAS teardown of qte77/agentic-job-offer-to-application-kit (2026-06-30) rated the repo HIGH with 10 findings. Verified triage outcome: **1 confirmed** (severity overstated for the deployment context), **1 hardening kernel**, **8 false positives — 2 outright fabricated** (a `sed` command in a Makefile that contains none; the XXE *defense* `defusedxml` and the traversal *sanitizer* `safe_slug` flagged as the vulnerabilities).
